solar-elevation.short: How high the Sun stands above the horizon, in degrees: 0° at sunrise and sunset, 90° straight overhead.

solar-zenith-angle.short: The angle between the Sun and the point straight overhead. It is 90° minus the solar elevation.

solar-azimuth.short: The compass direction of the Sun, in degrees clockwise from north: 90° east, 180° south, 270° west.

solar-declination.short: The latitude where the Sun is directly overhead at noon. Because Earth's axis is tilted, it swings between about +23.4° in June and −23.4° in December, passing 0° at the equinoxes.

solar-time.short: Time set by the Sun rather than by time zones: the Sun crosses due north or south at about 12:00 solar time. Clocks can differ from it by an hour or more.

equation-of-time.short: How far a sundial runs ahead of or behind an even clock, up to about 16 minutes, because Earth's orbit is an ellipse and its axis is tilted.

direct-normal-irradiance.short: Sunlight coming straight from the Sun's disc, measured on a surface turned to face the Sun square on, in W/m².

diffuse-horizontal-irradiance.short: Sunlight scattered by air, haze and clouds that arrives from the rest of the sky, measured on a flat horizontal surface, in W/m².

global-horizontal-irradiance.short: All the sunlight reaching flat, level ground: the direct beam times the cosine of the zenith angle, plus the diffuse light. Weather stations usually measure this.

plane-of-array-irradiance.short: The sunlight landing on the face of a tilted panel, in W/m²: the direct beam plus the share of sky light and ground reflection the panel can see.

insolation.short: Sunlight energy collected over a period, usually in kWh/m² per day or per year. Daily insolation in kWh/m² equals peak sun hours.

clear-sky-model.short: A formula for how much sunlight reaches the ground on a cloudless day. It gives a ceiling: real days with clouds and haze bring less.

isotropic-sky-model.short: The simplifying assumption that diffuse sky light is equally bright from every part of the sky, so a tilted panel collects it in proportion to how much sky it can see.

typical-meteorological-year.short: A year of hourly weather stitched together from real months that are typical for a site, used to estimate long-run solar output.
